payload.summary: RE-SCOPED: the timeout premise is falsified; the fault is the quality-retry ladder missing budget admission control
payload.detail: RE-SCOPED 2026-08-22 -- THE MECHANISM IN THIS ROW'S TITLE IS WRONG; READ docs/rag-improvement/231-diagnosis-2026-08-22.md BEFORE ACTING. This detail merges two records that were queued against this row independently and agree: the Phase 5 close-out latency measurement (queued 2026-08-21 as request 0a0ab127, cancelled in favour of this merged record with its content carried forward in full below) and the Gate E answer-level diagnosis of 2026-08-22. PART A -- PHASE 5.2 CONFIRMED SATISFIED with fresh data 2026-08-22 Perth (2026-08-21 UTC), not reopened. This row already recorded that remediation-plan Phase 5.2 is satisfied by S1's 2026-08-17 healthy-latency probes; the Phase 5 close-out re-measured production end to end and confirms it. Retrieval now costs 955 ms on the text fast path and 6720 ms on hybrid (from 31610 ms and 21757 ms at the incident), against answerRouteBudgetMs.fast of 25000 ms -- so retrieval consumes 4-27 percent of the fast budget and is no longer capable of binding it. The 2026-08-14 verdict that pre-generation latency WAS the binding cause stands for that window and is now closed out. Residual R4 is generation-side and unchanged; no separate R4 row was created, per this row's own instruction. The recommended-execution-queue row for this issue still presents it as A1 immediate approved live investigation with the old framing, which contradicts the P1 to P2 re-grade; re-grade the queue entry to P2 and re-scope it to the generation-side residual at reconcile, so the queue stops advertising a retrieval investigation the measurements have closed. PART B -- THE ANSWER-LEVEL DIAGNOSIS, measured offline against the 60 real answers of the Gate E capture of 2026-08-21 (output/gate-e/dump-v18.json at 4ea310e48 and dump-v19.json at cdfcbaccd, 30 cases each, gitignored, never committed), with every code claim re-verified at 226bd32cc. Part A's numbers and Part B's agree: with retrieval down to 955-6720 ms there is 16-22 s of a 25 s fast budget left for generation, which is enough for ONE attempt and not for the retry the quality ladder then launches. THREE FINDINGS. (1) The stated premise is false: answerRouteBudgetMs.fast binds in 3 of 60 case-runs. Budgets are fixed at route selection (createAnswerRouteDeadline is called once at rag.ts:2839 with the mode chooseAnswerRoute returned), and mapping each provider_timeout to its first routing token puts three of six on the 35s STRONG budget (benzodiazepine-agitation-dose v18 clinical_risk_or_complex_query; quetiapine-dose and mirtazapine-dose v19 medication_dose_risk_strong_route) and three on the 25s fast budget. Note strong_routine_retrieval is mode fast despite the name (rag-routing.ts:1288). Raising the fast budget cannot reach the strong-route half. (2) The defect population is 9-10 of 30, not ~20. answer_quality_tier source_only is a presentation label covering three unrelated populations: 12 of 30 cases never call the provider at all (provider_attempted false, identical both runs), 1 is a correct abstention, and only 9 (v18) and 10 (v19) are generation-attempted-then-discarded. Of the 8 identical plain source_only cases, 4 are CORRECT (they literally ask which documents support X and receive a document list, routed source_support_document_lookup with no fallback token in the chain), 2 answer a clinical question with a document list (duress-pathway, agitation-im-route), and 2 ship incoherent prose. (3) provider_timeout and generation_quality_failed are ONE fault -- the quality-retry ladder -- wearing two labels, and the label only records whether the ladder ran out of wall-clock or out of retries. lamotrigine-rash-action carries the same gate reason missing_query_overlap under BOTH labels across the two runs; mirtazapine-dose v19 is labelled provider_timeout while carrying bad_final_answer_quality with one response; the delivered answer is byte-identical either way; and the two runs' timeout sets have zero overlap on identical inputs. Root cause: the quality escalations fast_quality_retry_strong (rag.ts:3623, generating at 3660) and strong_quality_retry (rag.ts:3709, generating at 3721) call generateWithModel with NO deadline admission check -- deadlineAllowsGenerationRetry is wired only to the truncation self-heal at rag.ts:3542 -- and the one time-guard that exists (rag.ts:3698) compares against generationTotalBudgetMs of 60000 ms inside a 35 s route deadline, so it can never fire. This is residual R1, still open for every class except dosing. 34 percent (v18) and 48 percent (v19) of input tokens bought answers the pipeline then discarded. NEW DEFECT FOUND, FILED AS ITS OWN ROW: a GROUNDED first-choice extractive answer is never quality-checked, because generatedAnswerQualityFailureReason is called only inside the !finalizedAnswer.grounded branch at rag.ts:3107. The two worst answers in the whole capture are grounded and therefore carry no fallback_reason, no gate reason and degraded_mode.active false, so every metric built on fallback_reason -- including this row's framing and the Gate E blinded tally -- scored them as clean. RE-SCOPED NEXT STEP for this row: add deadline admission control to the two quality retries and recalibrate the dead 60 s guard; expected effect is the same answer returned sooner with less discarded spend, not more model answers. The route-budget stop condition is UNCHANGED and this diagnosis reinforces it -- do not raise answerRouteBudgetMs. Protected surface; needs a live eval-canary pair. NOT ESTABLISHED OFFLINE: the dumps carry no latency fields, so how close any individual case came to its deadline is unmeasured (Part A bounds the retrieval share but not the per-case generation share); whether the two incoherent strings would actually trip a gate if one ran is unproven and is step 1 of the fix packet; two runs is not a distribution. A latency-instrumented re-capture and a repeat capture (about 0.66 USD each, estimated from token counts because estimated_cost_usd is null in both dumps) were both offered to the owner on 2026-08-22 and declined as unnecessary for the diagnosis. Open-PR check performed per #292: seven open PRs, none touching src/lib/rag/**. HANDOVER section 1's decisive-constraint paragraph still describes this row as a budget problem and needs a one-line pointer to the diagnosis; that edit was deliberately deferred because PR #2257 is modifying HANDOVER.md. PRIOR RECORD, UNCHANGED: S1 (#2022), S1b (#2035) and S1d (#2054) landed with green canary pairs, closing the generation-quality false rejections and the finalizer-gap hole. Live-drift #316 Phase 1.2 classified all ten RPC divergences as attribute-only, so canaries since 2026-08-14 measure a reconstructable path.
